newPackage.name: dsh-expense-claim-check
newPackage.theRuleThatEarnsIt: total-mismatch — a claim whose lines sum to 1,513.50 but whose total says 1,600.00 looks completely normal on the page: tidy numbers, aligned table, and the total is the number the approver actually reads
newPackage.secondHalf: invoice-duplicate — one claim, two lines, different dates, same invoice number; nobody counts digits
precisionChoices: invoice numbers and dates are stripped before amounts are parsed, or a 14-digit invoice number becomes a 73-trillion-yuan line item (this happened on the first smoke run)
amounts above ten million are treated as data errors, not summed
currency is compared by code, not spelling: bare 元 counts as CNY, and 美元/欧元 are matched and masked before it so their 元 is not misread

myOwnBugsDuringBuild.bug: `\b发票号码` never matched — the CJK word-boundary trap this kit had already documented twice
myOwnBugsDuringBuild.symptom: first smoke run reported invoice-missing on a claim full of invoice numbers
myOwnBugsDuringBuild.note: reintroduced in a brand-new package by the same author who wrote the note about it

myOwnBugsDuringBuild.bug: the period branch passed `/(?:^|\n)/` as its line fallback, which matches any text, so the whole branch was dead
myOwnBugsDuringBuild.symptom: date-missing and period-unlabelled could never fire; two tests caught it

myOwnBugsDuringBuild.bug: AMOUNT allowed at most two decimals, so a total written 1600.004 parsed as 4
myOwnBugsDuringBuild.fix: the tolerance test now expresses the difference as one cent, which is what the reader can represent

npxVerified: clean claim -> 0 errors 0 warnings, 3 items summing 1600
mismatched claim -> 2 errors 2 warnings, sum 1513.5 vs total 1600
processNote: the push loop grepped for 'main -> main' while git prints 'HEAD -> main', so six successful-looking failures were reported; the push had in fact landed. Same class as the earlier 'up-to-date' false green — the check was written against an imagined output format rather than the real one.
